about: Seventeen laws on hired animals and hired men. The first block is about oxen that are hired or seized: an ox seized as a pledge costs a third of a mina (§241); two kinds of hired ox or team, whose Sumerian names I cannot read, cost four and three kor of grain a year (§242–243). Then who bears the loss of a hired animal: its owner, if a lion kills it in the open country (§244); the hirer, who must replace the ox with an ox like it if he kills it through carelessness or a beating or breaks its foot (§245–246), half its price for its eye and a quarter for its horns, tail or flesh (§247–248); but not if a god strikes it, when his oath frees him (§249). Next the goring ox (§250–252): no claim if it gores a man as it goes along; but if it was known as a gorer, its owner was told and did nothing, and it kills a man’s son, he pays half a mina, and a third of a mina for a slave. The last block is the hired farm-steward (§253–256), put in charge of a field with supplies and cattle: if he is caught stealing seed or fodder his hands are cut off; if he weakens the cattle he makes up the grain; if he hires the cattle out or grows no crop he measures out sixty kor for every ten bur; and if he cannot pay he is dragged about the field with the cattle. The part ends with a hired man’s wage, eight kor of grain a year (§257). Several words are not readable from the grammar and I say so in the notes: the two named oxen (§242–243), labiānu and pasuttu (parts of the ox), aldāʾam, tâna, pīḫatu, the hired man’s title AK.ŠU, and some verbs (ittasak, ušarrim, imtanaššarūšu). Col. XXXVI ends at line 91 and col. XXXVII runs to line 101; Harper’s line numerals agree with his own section headings throughout.

sentences.n: Here the laws on hired and seized animals and on hired men begin (§241–257: oxen §241–252, the hired field-steward §253–256, a hired man §257). The usual šumma pattern: šumma awīlum … “if a man …”, the condition in the perfect, the penalty in the present. alpam is the one sign GU₄ “ox”, with no -am written (on the plate the same word is sometimes GU₄ alone and sometimes GU₄ + the sign AM; I note which each time). ana nibūtim ittebi: ittebi is the perfect of nebûm “to distrain, seize as a pledge” and nibūtim “as a hostage (for debt)”; both words are as in §114–116, where a person is the pledge; here it is an ox. The sense “seize an ox for a debt” is Harper’s; it is what the penalty in the next line fits.

sentences.i: If a man has hired an ox or a donkey, and a lion has killed it in the open country,
sentences.n: Two animals are listed without “or”: alpam imēram īgurma “has hired an ox, a donkey, and”. ina ṣērim “in the open country” (the steppe, as in §17). UR.MAḪ is the two signs UR “dog” + MAḪ “great” and means “lion”; I write nēšum, but labbum is also “lion” and the signs do not choose (Harper prints MAH with a plain H). iddūkšu (id-du-uk-šu) is read as “has killed him/it”: the perfect of dâkum “to kill” with -šu “him/it”, the doubled d being the perfect’s infix -ta- assimilated to the root’s d, the middle ʾ contracted to ū (the perfect is the tense of the protasis throughout the code; elsewhere Harper writes i-du-uk, as in idukkū, for the present); UNCERTAIN in form, as the stem vowels are only read from the shape. sentences.i: If a man has hired an ox and has broken its horns, cut off its tail, or torn off (?) the flesh of its pasuttu (?),
sentences.n: Three injuries in a row: išbir “has broken” (preterite of šebērum) with qarnīšu “its horns” (the form is oblique, a plural or dual, so “horns”); ittakis “has cut” with zibbassu “its tail” (Harper’s zibba-zu: the logogram ZIB, zibbatum “tail”, + the sign ZU standing for -ssu, as in nibūssu); then ulu šīr pasuttišu ittasak. šīr is the logogram SU “flesh” (šīrum; Harper’s sign no. 80, šēru). pasuttum is written with two signs, not syllabically: Harper’s List of Signs (no. 50) gives it as the corner sign SA plus a second sign and calls it pasuttu, a part of the ox that I cannot read. The second sign (a triangle with a small diamond in it and a long tail wedge) I could not identify; it is keyed UL only as the nearest shape. On the plate row (XXXVII 32) the triangle sign stands before the corner sign, between SU and šu, where Harper’s List prints SA first; the glyphs follow the plate, so the reading is X.SA (X = the unidentified sign), and the order is UNCERTAIN along with the whole word. ittasak (it-ta-sa-ak) is the perfect of nasākum “to throw, cast”; “tear off” is a guess from the sense, UNCERTAIN: the sign AK could also be aq, nasāqum “to pick out”. sentences.i: If an ox, going along the street (?), has gored a man and killed him,
sentences.n: The goring-ox laws (§250–252). alpum here is GU₄ + um (the subject of the clause). zu-ga-am (Harper’s zugam) is a word I cannot place with confidence. What the grammar allows: an accusative ending -am, followed by ina alākišu “in its going”, so a word for a place or way the ox went along. If zu stands for su (z for s is not rare in Old Babylonian spelling) and ga for qa₂, the word is sūqam “street”, an accusative of the way gone (alākum with a road for its object): “as it goes along the street”. UNCERTAIN: the spelling with z is not confirmed, and the rendering rests on this. Other words of the shape zuq- (a form of zuqtum, “peak”) would show a t, which is not written here. ina alākišu “in its going” (alākum “to go”, the infinitive with -šu). ikkipma: Harper prints ik-ki-ib-ma, but the sign IB also has the value ip (his List of Signs no. 186, “ib, ip”) and the verb is nakāpum “to gore, butt” (as in munakkip, “gorer of”), so I say ikkipma (preterite + -ma), “has gored, and”; the reading with b is Harper’s. uštamīt is the Š-stem of mâtum, “has caused to die”.

glossary.aldāʾam: aldāʾam, a word I cannot read, UNCERTAIN, a form-lemma only: aldāʾam (Harper’s al-dá-a-am, accusative ending), taken as farm supplies entrusted to the steward (seed-grain?) from the context alone, left unread
glossary.alpum: ox (GU₄) · forms met: alpam (accusative, GU₄ alone or GU₄ + AM: GU₄-am), alpum (GU₄-um, subject), alpim (genitive, GU₄), alap (construct “ox of”: alap awīlim “a man’s ox”), alpīšu (GU₄-šu) “his ox”; the plate writes the word sometimes GU₄ alone and sometimes with a following sign
glossary.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak) · ittalak “she has gone” (perfect): ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” · ittalku (it-ta-al-ku) with the subjunctive -u: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate”
glossary.ana: to, for · with an infinitive, “to, for” (ana kirîm zaqāpim “to plant as an orchard”); “as” (ana kirîm), “into” (ana libbi), “at the rate of” (ana itêšu)
glossary.apālum: to answer; to satisfy, pay (a creditor): ippalma (present, with -ma) “he shall pay, and” · uppal (u-up-pa-al) “she shall pay”, taken as a present (a G present would be ippal; the u- is unexplained), in šaniam ul uppal, UNCERTAIN · apālam (a-pa-lam, infinitive, accusative) “to pay”: apālam lā ileʾʾi “he is not able to pay”
glossary.awīlum: man; the free citizen, the code’s first legal class
glossary.babtum: UNCERTAIN: Harper’s “loss, defects”, but in §126 apparently the party accused of the loss, “the one blamed” (later dictionaries have babtum as a city quarter or ward, which would be a group held liable): babtašu, babtišu (ba-ab-ta-šu, ba-ab-ti-šu) “his babtum”; the sense is not secure
glossary.bašûm-Š: Š-stem of bašûm “to exist”: to bring into being, produce (a crop): uštabši “he has produced” (perfect)
glossary.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading) · bēlišu (be-li-šu) “its owner” (of an animal), bēlišuma “to its owner only” (with the emphatic -ma); bēl alpim “the owner of the ox”
glossary.būrum: the bur, a field measure (written GAN.E; Harper reads GAN, 1,800 SAR, about 6⅔ acres): būrim
glossary.dâkum: to kill; N-stem iddâk “he shall be killed” — the code’s death sentence · idukkū (i-du-uk-ku) “they shall kill” (active plural, unlike the N-stem iddâk) · iddūkšu (id-du-uk-šu) “has killed him/it”, taken as the perfect + -šu, the doubled d being the perfect’s infix -ta- assimilated to the root’s d (so read; UNCERTAIN in form)
glossary.dīnum: case, lawsuit; judgment: dīn napištim “a case of life”
glossary.ebūrum: harvest, the crop: ebūrim “of harvest, at harvest” (one logogram, read BURU₁₄; Harper writes ebûrim)
glossary.edûm-Š: Š-stem (causative) of edûm “to know”: to make known, notify: ušēdišumma (u-še-di-šum-ma, preterite + -šum “to him” + -ma) “he made known to him, and”, written as a passive in English because no subject is named
glossary.enēšum-D: D-stem of enēšum “to be weak”: to weaken, make weak: utenniš (u-te-en-ni-iš, 3rd singular preterite; a D perfect would be uttenniš) “he has weakened”, said of cattle; the adjective enšum “weak” is in the prologue
glossary.eqlum: field (written A.ŠÀ): eqelšu “his field” — the fief-land this whole block protects · bound form eqel (eqel itêšu “his neighbour’s field”; eqel ušākilu “the field he grazed”) · eqlam (A.ŠÀ, accusative) “the field”, eqlša (A.ŠÀ-ša) “her field”: eqlša u kirâša “her field and her orchard” · eqlišu (A.ŠÀ-šu) “his field”, eqlim (A.ŠÀ-lim, genitive) “of the field, in the field”
glossary.erēšum: to ask, demand; also to cultivate: irriš “he demands (his field back)” · erēšim (e-ri-ši-im, infinitive, genitive) “to cultivate”: ana eqlim erēšim “to cultivate the field”
glossary.idum: hire, wages (Harper: ID, the ideogram for hire): idi našpakim “the hire of the bin”, written with the single sign Á (A₂, “arm; hire”); the case ending is not written, so idi (construct, before a genitive) is an assumed reading, UNCERTAIN · idīšu (Á-šu, with -šu “his”) “his fee”, the physician’s pay: ana asîm idīšu “to the physician as his fee”; the case vowel is UNCERTAIN · Á alone, no ending and no suffix written, before a named kind of ox: idi GU₄.DA.UR.RA “the hire of a GU₄.DA.UR.RA”; the plate sign is Á (A₂), where Harper prints ID
glossary.igrum: hire, wages: ana igrim ittadin “he hired (him) out”
glossary.ilum: god; here: the temple as owner · plural ilāni “gods” (written DINGIR.DINGIR, as in the litany): maḫar ilāni “before the gods”
glossary.imtanaššar: imtanaššar-, UNCERTAIN, a form-lemma for an unclear root: a Gtn present of a verb whose root I take as mašārum, a guess, “to drag about” (Harper’s sense): imtanaššarūšu (im-ta-na-aš-ša-ru-šu, present plural + -šu) “they shall drag him about (?)”; the -tan- gives “repeatedly”
glossary.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year” · “with, by”, of company or means (UNCERTAIN): ina liātim “with (or by) the cattle”
glossary.izuzzum: to stand; izzazzu “he stands (in service)” · izzaz, izzazma (i-za-az, i-za-az-ma) “she shall stand (take her place)”, of an heir’s share: zittam kīma aplim ištēn izzazma “she shall take a share like one heir, and”; ul izzaz “she shall have no share”; sense UNCERTAIN · mūzaz (mu-za-az) “one who stands (in service)”, the participle, construct before a genitive: mūzaz ekallim “one who stands in the palace’s service” · uzuzzim (u-zu-uz-zi-im, infinitive, genitive) “to stand (in charge)”: ana pani eqlišu uzuzzim “to take charge of his field”
glossary.išûm: to have: lā īšu “he has not” · īšu “he has”, īšû (the subjunctive form, in a clause that continues): ana turrim lā īšû “has not to repay”
glossary.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver” · with a spelled vowel after the logogram: KÙ.BABBAR-a-am, -i-im, -u-um: kaspam, kaspim, kaspum (accusative, genitive, nominative); kaspum as the subject; the grain-and-silver pair šeʾam u kaspam “grain and silver” · kasap (KÙ.BABBAR, no ending written) construct “silver of”: kasap tirḫatim “silver of the bride-price” · kaspi (KÙ.BABBAR, no complement written; Harper’s normalization) in kaspi mišil šīmišu “silver, half its price”
glossary.kurrum: the kor, a grain measure (written GUR; Harper: 300 KA): kur šeʾam “a kor of grain” · written GUR.É (the editors’ print GUR-É) as well as GUR: 1 GUR.É, kurrum “a kor” (UNCERTAIN: the .É is not explained here) · written ŠE.GUR.E, with a final E: ana 1 ŠE.GUR.E “for one kor (of grain)”; the .E is not explained here, UNCERTAIN
glossary.kânum-D: D-stem of kânum: to convict, prove against someone (uktīn, ukannūšuma) · uktīn (uk-ti-in, perfect, with the infixed -t-) “he has convicted”; ukannūšuma (u-ka-an-nu-šu-ma, present, plural, with -šu “him” and -ma) “they shall convict him, and”; ukānma (u-ka-an-ma, present, singular) “he shall convict, and” · ukannūšima (u-ka-an-nu-ši-ma) “they shall convict her, and”, present plural with -ši “her” and -ma
glossary.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost” · “in proportion to”: kīma emūq zittiša “in proportion to the strength of her share”, kīma emūq bīt abim “in proportion to the means of her father’s house”
glossary.labiān: labiān-, UNCERTAIN: a word I cannot read, a form-lemma only (no root identified); the law lists it beside the foot of a hired ox, so it is probably a part of the animal, but that is only the context: labiānšu (la-bi-a-an-šu) “its labiān-”, left untranslated
glossary.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took” · ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took, and” (preterite ilqe + -ma, here without a spelled e); ilteqe (il-te-qi₂, perfect) “he has taken”; ileqqi (i-li-qi₂, present) “he shall take”; leqîm (li-qi₂-im, infinitive, genitive): ina kaspim leqîm “in the taking of the silver” · ileqqûma (i-li-qu₂-ma) “they shall take, and” (present plural + -ma); ileqqēma “he shall take, and” · ileqqû (i-li-qu₂-u) “they shall take” (present plural, without -ma) · ilqi (il-qi₂) “he took”; ilqûšu (il-qu₂-u-šu) “(when) he took him”, with the subjunctive -u and -šu “him”; ilqûšuma (il-qu₂-šu-ma) “he took him, and” (with the subjunctive -u before -šu, after ša); ana tarbītim ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took (him) as a foster-child, and”
glossary.leʾûm: to be able: ileʾʾi “he is able” (Harper: i-li-i)
glossary.liātum: cattle: Harper’s LID.GUD.ZUN — the cow-sign, the ox-sign, and the plural marker (the stele carves ḪI+A)
glossary.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see”
glossary.lū: or; either (lū … lū “whether … or”); with verb: “let …” · ù lu, two words written together, “or”: ù lu ina maḫāṣim “or through beating”
glossary.madādum: to measure out (grain): imaddad “he shall measure out”
glossary.manûm: mina — weight of silver, 60 shekels (about 500 g): 1 mana kaspim · spelled in syllables, ma-na, at §59: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver”
glossary.marārum: to hoe, break clods: imarrar “he shall hoe” · imrirū (im-ri-ru, preterite plural, the ending -ū also serving as the subjunctive) “which they hoed”, UNCERTAIN: the vowel i is not what a preterite beside imarrar would give (imrurū), so the root is in doubt too
glossary.maḫāṣum: to strike; of ground, to break up: imaḫḫaṣ “he shall break up” · the noun maḫāṣum “beating, abuse, injury” (Harper), written ma-ḫa-ṣi-im with the sign ZI (value ṣi): maḫāṣim “(through) beating” · imtaḫaṣ (im-ta-ḫa-aṣ, perfect) “he has struck”, imḫaṣma (preterite + -ma), amḫaṣ “I struck”: amḫassu (am-ḫa-zu) “I struck him” (ṣ + š said ss, written with ZU); the infinitive maḫāṣišu (ma-ḫa-zi-šu) “his striking, his blow”, ina maḫāṣišu “from his blow” · imḫassuma (im-ḫa-zu-ma, preterite imḫaṣ + -šu “him” + -ma, ZU for -ssu) “has struck him, and”, of a god striking an animal dead
glossary.mišlum: half: ana mišlāni “for halves” (in halves) · mišil (mi-ši-il) “half of”, before a noun: mišil šīmišu “half his price”, mišil šīmiša “half her price”
glossary.mâtum: to die: imtūt (im-tu-ut, perfect) “he/she has died”, so ina šīmātīša imtūt “she died a natural death”
glossary.mâtum-Š: Š-stem (causative) of mâtum “to die”: to make die, to kill: uštamīt (uš-ta-mi-it, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has caused (him) to die” · Š-stem verb
glossary.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son” · mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons” (nominative plural + suffix); mārīša (DUMU-ša) “her son” (genitive + suffix): ana mārīša “to her son” · mārī (DUMU-i) “my son” (-ī “my”); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “children” in mārī ūlissum “children she bore him”; mārū (DUMU{meš}) “sons” as subject: mārū ana ummātim ul izuzzū “the sons shall not divide by mothers” · mār X (DUMU, the sign TUR) “a member of the class X”, literally “son of X”: mār ummiānim “a craftsman”, mār zinništim “the son of a woman”; māram (DUMU) “a son”, mārašu (DUMU-šu) “his son”, mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons”, mārīšu “his sons”
glossary.mēgūtum: carelessness, negligence (Harper’s sense; UNCERTAIN as a word, the sense is the one the law needs): ina mēgūtim (me-gu-tim) “through carelessness”
glossary.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her” · anaddin “I shall give”, with the n merged into the k of -kum: anaddikkum (a-na-ad-di-ik-kum) “I shall give (her) to you”; iddinu (id-di-nu) “(which) he gave”; iddinušum “he gave him” · nadānam (na-da-nam, infinitive accusative) “to give”: warkassa … nadānam “(that she may) give her estate” · iddišši (id-di-iš-ši) “he gave her”, preterite + -ši, the n written š: ana mutim iddišši “he gave her to a husband” · inaddinūši (i-na-ad-di-nu-ši) “they shall give her”, inaddinūšimma (i-na-ad-di-nu-šim-ma) “they shall give her, and”, ittadnūšimma (it-ta-ad-nu-ši-im-ma) “they have given her, and” (perfect plural + -šim + -ma) · iddinušim (id-di-nu-ši-im) “he gave her”, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause
glossary.nakkāpum: gorer, a goring (butting) ox (noun from nakāpum “to gore”): nakkāpamma (na-ak-ka-a[m-ma], the last signs restored; the exact form UNCERTAIN) “is a gorer” · nakkapû (na-ak-ka-pu-u) in kīma nakkapû “as a gorer”, the ending -û Harper’s, UNCERTAIN
glossary.nakāpum: to gore, butt; munakkip “gorer of” · ikkipma (Harper’s ik-ki-ib-ma, the sign IB read ip; preterite + -ma) “has gored, and”
glossary.nakāsum: to cut, cut down: ikkis (preterite) “he cut down” · inakkisū (i-na-ak-ki-su) “they shall cut off”, present plural (the ending -sū is written with the one sign su, as Harper prints it): lišānšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his tongue”, tulêša inakkisū “they shall cut off her breast” · inakkisū “they shall cut off”, of the hand(s) and the ear: rittēšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his hand(s)”, uznašu inakkisū “they shall cut off his ear” · ittakis (it-ta-ki-is, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has cut (off)”
glossary.nasākum: to throw, cast (UNCERTAIN in the sense used): ittasak (it-ta-sa-ak, perfect) “he has thrown”, taken as “has torn off” from the context; the final sign AK could also be aq, which would be nasāqum “to pick out”
glossary.nebûm: to distrain, seize as a pledge (Harper; later dictionaries write nepûm, with p): ittebi (it-te-bi, perfect) “he has distrained”; ibbima (ib-bi-ma, preterite + -ma) “he distrained, and” (Harper lists ib-bi under this verb); nēbīša (ne-bi-ša) “her distrainer”, the one who holds the hostage (a noun from the verb, with -ša; the exact shape of the noun is UNCERTAIN)
glossary.nibūtum: hostage for debt, a person taken as pledge (Harper: “hostage”; from nebûm; later dictionaries write nipûtum, with p, from nepûm): nibūtum, nibūtim; nibūssu (ni-bu-zu, the sign ZU standing for -ssu, nibūt + -šu) “his hostage”; ana nibūtim “for a hostage”
glossary.nēšum: lion — written with the two signs UR “dog” + MAḪ “great”: UR.MAḪ, said nēšum; labbum is also “lion” and the signs do not choose between them, UNCERTAIN which word is meant: ina ṣērim UR.MAḪ “a lion in the open country”
glossary.nīšum: oath (literally “life”): nīš ilim “the oath by the god”
glossary.paqādum: to entrust, care for; pāqid “caretaker” · ipqissum (ip-qi₂-zum, preterite ipqid + -šum, d + š said ss, ZUM for -ssum) “he has entrusted to him”
glossary.pasuttum: pasuttum, a part of an ox I cannot identify, UNCERTAIN: written with two signs, the corner sign SA and a triangle sign with a diamond and a tail that I could not identify (Harper’s List of Signs no. 50 gives the pair as pasuttu; on the plate the triangle sign comes first), + -šu: pasuttišu “its pasuttu”; šīr pasuttišu “the flesh of its pasuttu”
glossary.pānum: front, face: ina pani “in front of” · panīša ištakan “she has set her face”: the idiom for making up one’s mind, resolving to do something; with ana + infinitive “to …” (panīšu, panīša “his, her face”) · idioms: panam šakānum “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind; panīšu wabālum “to carry his face” = to overlook an offence (UNCERTAIN) · ana pani X uzuzzim “to stand before X”, i.e. to be in charge of it: ana pani eqlišu uzuzzim “to take charge of his field” (a reading from the sense, UNCERTAIN)
glossary.pīḫatum: pīḫatum, UNCERTAIN: Harper’s bi-ḫa-zu read as pīḫassu (pīḫatum + -šu, t + š said ss, ZU for -ssu) “his pīḫatu”, taken from the context as what he owes; a form-lemma, the root is not clear to me
glossary.qarnum: horn: qarnīšu (qar-ni-šu) “its horns” (an oblique plural or dual, so “horns”)
glossary.qiāpum: to entrust, give in trust (Harper “to intrust”, listed under qâpu): iqīp(ma) “he entrusted (the agent), and” · iqīpšu ([i]-qi₂-ip-šu, preterite + -šu, first sign restored, IB read ip) “he has entrusted to him”
glossary.qātum: hand: ina qāt “from the hand of” · qātīšu (qa₂-ti-šu) “of his hands”: bīš qātīšu “his own goods” · qāt (qa₂-at) construct “in the hand of, in the care of”: ina qāt mušēniqtim “in the care (hand) of the wet-nurse” · qātīšu “of his hands” in šipir qātīšu “the work of his hands” · ina qātišu (qa₂-ti-šu) “in his hand”: ittaṣbat ina qātišu “he was caught with it in his hand”
glossary.rakāsum-D: D-stem of rakāsum “to bind”: to bind (by agreement), contract with (Harper: “to contract with”): urtakkis (ur-ta-ak-ki-is, perfect, with the t of the perfect after the first sign); who the subject is rests on the context · urakkissu (u-ra-ak-ki-su, D with -šu) “he has bound him (to it)”, the final sign su read for -ssu, UNCERTAIN
glossary.rebûm: fourth: rebûtim šattim “in the fourth year” · rebūt (IGI.4.GAL) “one quarter”: rebūt šīmišu “a quarter of its price”; the spoken form is reconstructed, UNCERTAIN
glossary.rittum: hand: rittēšu (UM.ME-šu, the signs UM, ME and ŠU) “his hand(s)”, with -šu “his”; Harper normalizes rit-tê-šu with an ending -ê whose grammar is not clear to me; the second sign (read ME) and the number, one hand or two, are both UNCERTAIN · noun
glossary.sanāqum: to keep in check (UNCERTAIN: the sense is taken from the context alone): D-stem usanniqma (u-sa-an-ni-iq-ma, preterite + -ma) “he has (not) kept (it) in check, and”; alpīšu lā usanniqma “he has not kept his ox in check (?)”
glossary.sūqum: street, way (UNCERTAIN): sūqam (zu-ga-am, accusative) “the street”, reading zu for su and ga for qa₂; the z for s spelling is not confirmed
glossary.tâna: tâna, a word I cannot read, UNCERTAIN, a form-lemma only (Harper’s ta-a-na): it names something measured in grain (the loss, yield or amount?), left as tâna
glossary.ušarrim: ušarrim (u-šar-ri-im), a D-stem preterite (u-šarrim) of a verb whose root I cannot fix, UNCERTAIN, a form-lemma only; the sense “trim, cut back (the horns)” is what the context needs and nothing else supports: lā ušarrim “he has not trimmed (?)”
glossary.wardum: male slave (ARAD) · warad (ARAD, no ending written) “male slave of …”, wardam (ARAD-am)
glossary.wašārum: D-stem (w)uššurum “to release, set free”: ūtaššar “he shall be released” · the form ūtaššar (ū-ta-aš-šar) is the Dt, the t-form of the D-stem, in the present: “he shall be released”; the “D-stem” named above is the stem family, and this form is its t-form (Dt)
glossary.zakārum: to name, declare: izzakar “he named”, izakkarma “he shall declare, and”
glossary.zibbatum: tail (ZIB): zibbassu (ZIB-zu, the sign ZU standing for -ssu, zibbat + -šu, t + š said ss) “its tail”
glossary.zērum: seed; offspring (written with the seed-sign NUMUN) · zēr šeʾim (ŠE.ZIR, the logogram ŠE + ZIR) “seed-grain”
glossary.īnum: eye: īnšu … iššīma “he lifted his eye (to it)” — he coveted it · ša īnšu maḫru (i-in-šu) “whose eye is first” = the son he favours (UNCERTAIN idiom)
glossary.ŠÀ.GAL: ŠÀ.GAL, a Sumerogram of two signs, ŠÀ “heart, inside” + GAL “big”, which I cannot read; “fodder” is the guess from the pairing with seed-grain and cattle, UNCERTAIN: zēr šeʾim ù lu ŠÀ.GAL “seed-grain or fodder (?)” · Sumerogram, reading not given
glossary.šaqālum: to weigh out (silver = to pay): išqulu · išaqqal (present) “he shall weigh out”
glossary.šarāqum: to steal: išriq · išriqma (iš-ri-iq-ma, preterite + -ma) “he stole, and”
glossary.šattum: year: šattam (syllabic, §31) or MU (the year-sign, §30) · šattim (genitive); plural šanātim “years” (ša šanātim “of the years”); MU 4{kam}, said erbe šanātim “four years” · MU 3{kam}, said šalāš šanātim “for three years”; šanat (ša-na-at) “(in) the year”, ina šanat “each year”
glossary.šebērum: to break: ištebir (iš-te-bi-ir, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has broken”, išebbirū (i-še-ib-bi-ru, present, 3rd plural, with the b doubled) “they shall break” · verb · išbir (iš-bi-ir, preterite, 3rd singular) “he has broken”
glossary.šeʾum: barley, grain (the ŠE sign) · ŠE-am, ŠE-im, ŠE-um, written with the logogram and a spelled vowel; šeʾum as the subject; ŠE-am-ma “grain only” (with the restricting -ma); in broken forms še…
glossary.šumma: if — the word that opens every law of the code
glossary.šuāti: that, the aforesaid · as the independent pronoun “him”: šuāti u bīšašu “him and his goods”
glossary.šēpum: foot: šēpīšu (NER-šu, the one sign NER “foot” + šu) “his/its foot or feet”; the sign gives no number, so one foot or both is UNCERTAIN (Harper’s List of Signs no. 170, ner, kiš, šēpu)
glossary.šīmum: purchase, purchase price · šīmišu (ŠÁM-šu, with -šu “his”) “his price”, of a slave: mišil šīmišu “half of his price” · šīmiša (ŠÁM-ša, with -ša “her”) “her price”, of a boat: mišil šīmiša “half her price”; šīmišu “its price”, of an animal: rebūt šīmišu “a quarter of its price”
glossary.šīrum: flesh, body; wellbeing · šīr (SU, bound form before a genitive) “flesh of”: šīr pasuttišu “the flesh of its pasuttu”
glossary.ḫabātum-D: UNCERTAIN verb, the D-stem (intensive) of ḫabātum “to rob, plunder”, taken here as “to destroy” from the sense of the law, not from the grammar: uḫtabbit (uḫ-tab-bi-it, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has destroyed (?)”, said of an eye · D-stem verb, sense uncertain
glossary.ṣabātum-N: to be seized, caught (N-stem, passive of ṣabātum): iṣṣabit “she was caught” (preterite, in lā iṣṣabit); ittaṣbat “she was caught” (perfect)
glossary.ṣērum: the open country, the steppe: ina ṣērim “in the open country”
